answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy begins with binding each identity to costly, non-transferable work instead of a free address. Concretely, every new agent must submit a proof-of-work stamp plus a slashable bond, and its reputation counts only attestations co-signed by distinct peers in an auditable trust graph. When a thousand clones echo one answer, the graph merges them into a single cluster, so the delta between claimed and verified activity exposes the copies: a lone falcon cannot fake a flock, because no cluster's weight can exceed its unique staked collateral.
